summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives keyboard/mouse and privilege-bypassed Claude CLI on installer's host
details: cli.js opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound JSON messages to two sinks on the installer's machine: (a) nut-js keyboard/mouse/scroll input synthesis via handleInput(msg, w, h), and (b) askClaude(), which spawns the local `claude` CLI with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and a prompt supplied by the remote peer (run(bin, ["--continue", "-p", "--dangerously-skip-permissions", prompt]) triggered from ws.addEventListener("message",...) on ai_query / ai_voice_query messages). This gives whoever controls the relay arbitrary keystroke, pointer, and shell command execution on the host running the daemon, with Claude's permission prompts disabled. The same WebSocket also streams JPEG screen frames and PCM microphone audio to the hardcoded relay when the server reports viewers>0 (startStream / startAudioStream ws.send paths), so the installer's screen and audio content leave the machine to the same author-controlled endpoint. The relay hostname is hardcoded as the default and the daemon reconnects automatically, providing persistent remote access.
